children: U.S. energy firms likely added a below-normal 31 billion cubic feet of natural gas into storage last week, according to the average estimate in a Reuters poll released on Wednesday.
The estimate compares with an injection of 50 bcf during the same week a year ago and an average increase for that week of 37 bcf over the past five years (2021 to 2025).
In the prior week ended August 21, energy firms added 15 bcf of gas into storage. (USOILN=ECI)

If correct, the forecast for the week ended August 28 would increase stockpiles to 3.215 trillion cubic feet. That would be about 1.5% below the same week a year ago and about 5.3% above the five-year average for the week.
The U.S. Energy Information Administration is scheduled to release its weekly storage report at 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 GMT) on Thursday.
There were 92 total degree days (TDDs) last week, above the 30-year normal of 79 TDDs for the period, data from financial firm LSEG showed.
Total degree days measure the number of degrees a day's average temperature is above or below 65 degrees Fahrenheit (18 degrees Celsius) to estimate demand to cool or heat homes and businesses.
Reuters polled 10 analysts, whose estimates ranged from injections of 21 bcf to 40 bcf, with a median increase of 31 bcf.
Early estimates for the week ending September 4 showed an average increase of 25 bcf.
That figure compares with an injection of 69 bcf during the same week last year and a five-year average increase of 52 bcf.
